reason: The text explicitly demonstrates agency by both leaders AND common people. While leaders like Jeshua, Zerubbabel, and the priests direct the reconstruction efforts, the text repeatedly shows the people (עַם) exercising their own agency: they gather together ('וַיֵּאָסְפוּ הָעָם כְּאִישׁ אֶחָד'), participate in offering sacrifices, observe the festival, and most significantly, actively respond with emotional and vocal expressions ('וְכָל־ הָעָם הֵרִיעוּ תְרוּעָה גְדוֹלָה' - 'and all the people shouted a great shout'). The passage distinguishes between priestly/leadership functions and popular participation, showing that both groups have meaningful agency in the religious and communal activities described.
